issues.description: Field: SealSaloon.stock — The problem statement (lines 70-71) instructs students to initialize the SealSaloon attributes (including the stock) in the instance constructor: "These should be initialized ... in the constructor of `SealSaloon`". Later in the problem statement (lines 77-81) it explicitly requires that the stock attribute must be static and final (shared across instances). A static final field cannot be initialized in an instance constructor (it must be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer). The reference solution declares and initializes the field as a static final at declaration. This contradiction between where and how `stock` should be initialized (constructor vs declaration/static initializer) will confuse students about the correct declaration and initialization location for the stock field.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the requirement consistent. Option A (preferred to match the solution): specify that the SealSaloon.stock field is static final and must be initialized at declaration (or in a static initializer), and remove the instruction to initialize it in the instance constructor. Option B: if you want stock to be an instance final field initialized in the constructor, remove the static/final requirement from the problem statement and update the UML. Update the problem text and UML so they consistently state whether `stock` is static final (shared) or an instance field.

issues.description: Field: SealSaloon.totalOrders — The UML in the problem statement declares totalOrders as an int (UML line shows `-totalOrders: int`), but the reference implementation declares the field as a long (`private long totalOrders = 0;`). This type mismatch between the specification and the solution may confuse students about which numeric type to use for the field.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose a single type and make all artifacts consistent. If very large counts are unnecessary, update the solution to use int for `totalOrders` (or update the UML/problem text to indicate `long` if larger counts are intended). Prefer using `int` in the problem statement and solution unless you expect totalOrders to exceed Integer.MAX_VALUE.
